items.usage: Move to a clearance or approach position without cutting feed.
items.notes: Axes can move independently at their rapid rates, so the path may not be a straight line. Verify clearance before every rapid.

items.usage: Cut a straight line at the programmed feed rate.
items.notes: Feed interpretation depends on the active feed mode, units, and machine setup.

items.params: X Z I K or R
items.usage: Cut a clockwise arc in the active turning plane.
items.notes: Arc direction is viewed in the active plane. I/K or R rules and full-circle support vary by control.

items.params: X Z I K or R
items.usage: Cut a counterclockwise arc in the active turning plane.
items.notes: Arc direction is viewed in the active plane. I/K or R rules and full-circle support vary by control.

items.usage: Sets the normal turning plane for lathe arcs and canned cycles.
items.notes: Usually the default plane on a standard two-axis lathe.

items.usage: Select or verify inch programming units for the active control.
items.notes: On Haas controls, G20 checks that Setting 9 is Inch; it does not convert stored coordinates. Other controls may behave differently.

items.usage: Select or verify metric programming units for the active control.
items.notes: On Haas controls, G21 checks that Setting 9 is Metric; it does not convert stored coordinates. Other controls may behave differently.

items.description: Reference return through an intermediate point
items.params: U W or X Z, control-dependent
items.usage: Returns one or more axes toward machine reference using the control's defined format.
items.notes: Coordinates on the G28 block can create an intermediate move. Verify axis selection and clearance; G28 is not automatically a safe retract.

items.usage: Cancels active tool nose compensation before a safe exit or tool change.
items.notes: Use a deliberate lead-out clear of the part before or while canceling tool-nose compensation, following the control manual.

items.description: Spindle speed clamp or coordinate function, control-dependent
items.usage: Commonly limits maximum RPM when using constant surface speed on Fanuc-style lathes.
items.notes: G50 has different meanings on some controls. Verify the machine manual.

items.usage: Select the stored G54 work offset as the programmed part-zero reference.
items.notes: G54 selects stored values; it does not measure or set part zero. Work offsets and tool offsets are different.

items.usage: Finishes a profile previously defined by sequence blocks.
items.notes: Often used after G71 or G72. Exact behavior depends on the control.

items.params: U R P Q W F, format varies
items.usage: Removes material in repeated roughing passes along a defined profile.
items.notes: One-line and two-line formats differ. Never copy a format without matching the machine control.

items.params: W R P Q U F, format varies
items.usage: Removes material in repeated facing passes across a defined profile.
items.notes: Parameter letters and cycle format vary by control.

items.description: Peck drilling or face-grooving cycle, control-dependent
items.params: R Z Q F or control-specific format
items.usage: Used for repeated pecking or grooving motion depending on the machine.
items.notes: This code is especially control-specific. Verify the manual before use.

items.params: R X Z P Q F or control-specific format
items.usage: Commonly used for OD or ID grooving with repeated pecks on Fanuc-style controls.
items.notes: Cycle meaning and parameter format vary.

items.params: P Q R X Z F, format varies
items.usage: Cuts a thread over multiple controlled passes.
items.notes: One-line and two-line formats differ significantly by control generation.

items.usage: Automatically changes spindle RPM as cutting diameter changes.
items.notes: Use the machine's verified maximum-RPM limit where the procedure requires one.

items.usage: Runs the spindle at a fixed commanded RPM.
items.notes: Use constant RPM when required by the verified process and controller procedure.

items.usage: Selects feed per minute or feed per revolution on many turning controls.
items.notes: Haas lathes use G98 for feed per minute and G99 for feed per revolution; other control families may assign different codes.
